questions.q: What does "time to first token" (TTFT) measure?
options: The total time for a complete response to finish streaming
How long the user waits before any output token appears
The gap between the second and third output tokens
The time it takes the model to load into GPU memory
questions.explain: TTFT is the latency until the very first output token is produced — the wait before the user sees anything at all.

questions.q: A server generates the same total tokens/sec whether 40 users each feel the response was snappy or sluggish. What does this illustrate?
options: Throughput measures total system work, not any individual request's experience
Throughput and latency always move in the same direction
Tokens/sec is not a valid throughput unit for LLMs
Latency cannot be measured for concurrent users
questions.explain: Throughput is a system-wide total; it says nothing about how fast any single request felt, which is what latency measures.

questions.q: Why does increasing batch size typically raise both throughput and latency at the same time?
options: Larger batches always use a smaller, faster model
Requests in a larger batch share GPU compute and may wait for the batch to fill, even as more total work gets done per pass
Batching has no effect on GPU utilization
Larger batches reduce the number of tokens each request needs
questions.explain: Batching raises total throughput by processing more work per GPU pass, but each request in that batch shares compute and may wait to be collected, raising its own latency.

questions.q: Which metric tends to climb fastest as batch size grows, and is usually the real constraint in production?
options: Average (mean) latency
Median (p50) latency
Tail latency (p99)
Time to first token for the very first request of the day
questions.explain: Median latency creeps up slowly with batch size, but tail latency (p99) — the slowest requests — climbs much faster and is usually what production SLOs actually have to respect.

questions.q: For an interactive coding copilot versus a nightly batch summarization job, which metric should each prioritize?
options: Both should prioritize throughput equally
The copilot should prioritize low latency (especially TTFT); the batch job should prioritize throughput
The copilot should prioritize throughput; the batch job should prioritize latency
Neither metric matters once a GPU is fast enough
questions.explain: A live copilot has an impatient user waiting in real time, so low latency (especially TTFT) matters most. A nightly batch job has no one watching, so maximizing tokens/sec per dollar (throughput) matters most.
